title: Backflow preventer types: identify the family before you search for a fix
description: A device-family decision page covering why RPZ, double-check, vacuum-breaker, and other assemblies should be identified from the actual label and use case.
prompt: Which family is actually installed and what does that identification unlock?
answer: Device type identification should begin with the manufacturer label, model, size, and application. A family name is useful for routing but does not prove part compatibility or compliance status.
urgency: Escalate uncertain identity, active discharge, a failed test, or a proposed replacement before using a generic category.
diagramAlt: Backflow assembly shown as a device-family identification reference
identifiers: Label and nominal size are stronger evidence than visual similarity.
System use helps route the next question but does not replace the label.
Different device families have different service, installation, and test paths.

choices.label: I can see the model label
choices.detail: Use the exact model and size to find compatible service information.

choices.label: The device is on irrigation
choices.detail: Check the irrigation-specific assembly and freeze/access context.

choices.label: I see a relief or vent discharge
choices.detail: Treat relief discharge as a symptom to document, not a device type by itself.

steps.title: Establish the governing record
steps.body: Capture the whole assembly and all visible markings.

steps.title: Define the complete work
steps.body: Match the record to manufacturer documentation and actual system use.

steps.title: Document completion
steps.body: Route to the relevant test, repair, or installation requirement.

safeChecks: Use the exact property and assembly record before authorizing work.

stopConditions: The model cannot be confirmed before parts are selected.
A generic category is being used to approve replacement.
notThisDevice: A pressure regulator controls pressure and is a different product category.
A sewer backwater valve is not a potable-water backflow assembly.
A generic check valve does not establish a testable backflow preventer type.
